title: Hanoi vs Ho Chi Minh City vs Da Nang for teachers (2026)
description: Jobs, hourly pay, rent, climate and daily life in Saigon, Hanoi and Da Nang, compared with July–October 2026 job ads and rent data, and who each city suits.
h1: Hanoi vs Ho Chi Minh City (and Da Nang): which city should you teach in?
intro: Ho Chi Minh City is the easiest place to start: it is Vietnam's biggest market for English teachers by a wide margin, with heat all year and the highest city-centre rents. Hanoi pays the same or slightly more per hour in 2026 job ads and rent is cheaper, but it has a cool, damp winter and much worse winter air. Da Nang pays similar hourly rates with far fewer jobs, and some chains want three or more years' experience there.
keyPoints: **Job volume**: Ho Chi Minh City had 1,961 licensed language and IT centres in August 2025, plus public-school programmes, bilingual and international schools. Hanoi is the clear second market; Da Nang, Hai Phong, Nha Trang and Can Tho are small.

**Pay barely differs by city**: in July–October 2026 ads, Saigon centres offered {{vnd:390000-600000}} an hour (most new-teacher offers {{vnd:430000-560000}}), Hanoi {{vnd:550000-650000}} and Da Nang {{vnd:500000-570000}}.

**Rent is the big cost gap**: Numbeo puts a city-centre one-bedroom at {{vnd:15220000}} a month in Saigon, {{vnd:13630000}} in Da Nang and {{vnd:10600000}} in Hanoi; ordinary local-market one-bedrooms in Saigon are much cheaper ({{vnd:6800000}} median on the eno.vn Rent Index, October 2026).
**Climate decides it for many**: Saigon is hot all year with a rainy season; Hanoi has a cold, damp winter with smog; Da Nang and Nha Trang face storms and floods from about September to December.
**A job tagged 'Ho Chi Minh City' may not be in Saigon**: since 1 July 2025 the city includes Binh Duong and Ba Ria–Vung Tau. Always ask for the campus address.

sections.title: Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi and Da Nang side by side

blocks.text: The table puts the figures that matter in one place. Pay comes from 2026 job ads, which are snapshots rather than surveys; there is no official city-level pay data for foreign teachers. Rents and living costs come from [Numbeo](https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/in/Ho-Chi-Minh-City), which is crowd-sourced and leans towards the kind of flats expats rent.

blocks.text: On Numbeo's [2026 mid-year cost-of-living index](https://www.numbeo.com/cost-of-living/rankings.jsp?title=2026-mid) (New York = 100, rent excluded), Ho Chi Minh City scores 29.6, Hanoi 28.3 and Da Nang 27.2. The day-to-day gap between the three is small; rent is where your choice of city really shows.

sections.title: Why most teaching jobs are in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi

blocks.text: Teaching jobs follow paying learners, and most of them live in the two big cities. After the 1 July 2025 merger with Binh Duong and Ba Ria–Vung Tau, [Ho Chi Minh City has about 14 million people](https://www.sggp.org.vn/thanh-lap-tphcm-moi-post801737.html). In August 2025 its education department counted [1,961 licensed foreign-language and IT centres](https://daibieunhandan.vn/tp-ho-chi-minh-nang-cao-chat-luong-nhan-su-tai-cac-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-tin-hoc-10388655.html) (language and IT centres are counted together), which taught about 268,580 learners in 2024–25. In June 2020, the latest count we found, Hanoi's education department listed [947 licensed language centres](https://hoatieu.vn/phap-luat/danh-sach-trung-tam-ngoai-ngu-duoc-cap-phep-o-ha-noi-202536). We found no official count of foreign English teachers for any city.

Saigon also has the most kinds of employer. Agencies place foreign teachers in public schools, the city's integrated maths, science and English programme is taught by foreign teachers, and in June 2026 the city approved a 2026–2030 pilot letting [246 public preschools and schools contract foreign teachers directly](https://giaoduc.net.vn/tphcm-246-truong-mam-non-pho-thong-duoc-tu-tuyen-giao-vien-hop-dong-voi-giao-vien-nuoc-ngoai-post260905.gd). Hanoi is starting its own English-as-a-second-language pilots at 20 institutions in 2026–27. The [eno.vn school directory](/schools) lists Ho Chi Minh City's language centres, international schools and other employers, if you want to see the range.

Volume matters more than it looks. Hourly timetables can shrink, centres close (HCMC [dissolved or revoked 112 language and IT centres](https://vietnamnet.vn/en/ho-chi-minh-city-shuts-down-112-language-and-it-centers-2556885.html) in 2025–26), and contracts end. In a big market you can change employer without changing city. For the full picture of the Saigon market, read [teaching English in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/teaching-english-in-ho-chi-minh-city).

blocks.title: A 'Ho Chi Minh City' job may be hours from Saigon
blocks.text: Since 1 July 2025, Ho Chi Minh City includes the former Binh Duong and Ba Ria–Vung Tau provinces, Con Dao island among them, so a job tagged 'HCMC' can be 30 to 200+ km from District 1. Job boards also mislabel: on 10 October 2026 [a leading board](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs) listed a VUS campus in Vinh Long, a separate province, under Hồ Chí Minh. Before you accept, ask for the campus address with its new ward or commune name and map the commute.

sections.title: What teachers earn in each city

blocks.text: In 2026 ads Hanoi pays the same as Saigon or slightly more. Older claims that Saigon pays 10–15% more are not supported by current ads. Most ads do not say whether a rate is gross or net, and 'up to' figures are ceilings, so treat every number below as a starting point for questions.

blocks.caption: Advertised hourly and monthly pay for foreign English teachers by city, from job ads dated July–October 2026 (Ho Chi Minh City agency rates include some 2025 ads).

blocks.text: Sources: [ILA's Ho Chi Minh City ad](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/ila-is-hiring-part-time-esl-teachers-in-ho-chi-minh-city), [the 2026–27 public-school agency ad](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/foreign-esl-teachers-for-public-schools-in-ho-chi-minh-city-2026-2027/), [Sakura Schools Hanoi](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/hanoi-vietnam-english-teacher-sakura-schools-november-2026-start), [VN Education Hanoi](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/secondary-esl-full-time-native-english-teacher-in-hanoi) and [Fisher's Superkids Da Nang](https://vietnamteachingjobs.com/jobs/view/danang-vietnam-part-time-esl-teacher-needed-for-reputable-english-center-1).

A full-time centre load is about 78–95 contact hours a month, which at {{vnd:450000-550000}} an hour comes to roughly {{vnd:35000000-52000000}} gross a month. Income tax and social insurance are national rules, so the same gross gives the same net in every city; the [salary guide](/teach-in-vietnam/english-teacher-salary-in-vietnam) works through take-home pay under the 2026 tax rules.

The catch outside the big two is entry level. ILA's 2026 postings [require at least 3 years' teaching experience](https://www.theteflacademy.com/blog/tefl-jobs/full-time-esl-efl-teachers-needed-across-vietnam/) for its Da Nang, Nha Trang and Vung Tau centres, so a new teacher should not count on a beach-city placement with ILA, and should check experience requirements with any other employer there.

sections.title: Rent and the cost of living in each city

blocks.text: On Numbeo, Hanoi is the cheapest of the three for a central one-bedroom ({{vnd:10600000}} a month) and Saigon the dearest ({{vnd:15220000}}). Da Nang is not the cheapest for rent: its central one-bedrooms ({{vnd:13630000}}) cost more than Hanoi's because of demand near the beach, and outside the centre its one-bedrooms ({{vnd:8960000}}) are the dearest of the three, although its day-to-day costs are a little lower. Numbeo had 109 contributors for Ho Chi Minh City, 86 for Hanoi and 73 for Da Nang, so read these as indicative.

Numbeo's 'city centre' figure mostly reflects serviced flats aimed at expats. For Saigon there is a larger sample: the [eno.vn HCMC Rent Index](/hcmc-rent-index), built from 15,141 asking-price listings (snapshot 10 October 2026). It shows what ordinary local-market homes cost by district. Its city-wide medians were {{vnd:3900000}} a month for a room, {{vnd:6800000}} for a one-bedroom and {{vnd:13000000}} for a two-bedroom.

The two sources measure different things, so compare like with like: Numbeo across cities, the Rent Index within Saigon. Since July 2025 official addresses use new ward names (Thao Dien is now part of An Khanh ward), but listings and teachers still use the old districts. For budgets and neighbourhoods, see [the cost of living in Ho Chi Minh City](/teach-in-vietnam/cost-of-living-in-ho-chi-minh-city-for-teachers) and [where to live in Saigon](/teach-in-vietnam/where-to-live-in-ho-chi-minh-city-as-a-teacher).

sections.title: Climate: Hanoi winters, Saigon heat and rain, Da Nang storms

blocks.text: Climate is the difference you feel every day, and it often decides the choice.

items: **Ho Chi Minh City** is hot all year with no cold season. The rainy season runs roughly May to November, usually as heavy afternoon or evening downpours that flood some streets briefly. Air-conditioning is a real cost: it is what drives a Saigon electricity bill up.

**Hanoi** has a hot, wet summer and a cool, damp winter, roughly December to February. Homes usually have no central heating, so you feel the cold indoors too. Winter also brings Hanoi's worst air: measured fine-particle pollution (PM2.5) is much worse than Saigon's, especially from November to March. Teachers who live there commonly run an air purifier, keep N95 masks and check IQAir daily.

**Da Nang** has a milder winter than Hanoi, but September to December is storm and flood season. Central Vietnam, including Hoi An (now part of Da Nang city), had record floods in October–November 2025. Avoid ground-floor rentals on flood-prone streets.
**Nha Trang** shares the central coast's September–December storm and flood risk.

blocks.text: Numbeo's perception-based pollution scores are high for both big cities ([Ho Chi Minh City 92.1, Hanoi 89.0](https://www.numbeo.com/quality-of-life/rankings.jsp?title=2026-mid)), which hides the measured winter gap. If you have asthma or another breathing condition, weigh Hanoi's winter air seriously. Public schools nationwide follow one Ministry of Education framework: the year opens on 5 September and ends before 31 May; [the teaching year guide](/teach-in-vietnam/the-teaching-year-in-vietnam) covers terms, Tet and the rainy season.

On Numbeo's [2026 mid-year quality-of-life data](https://www.numbeo.com/quality-of-life/rankings.jsp?title=2026-mid), Hanoi scores better than Ho Chi Minh City on perceived safety (66.2 against 50.2) and on commute times (27.7 against 32.1). These are perceptions from contributors, not crime statistics; for what actually goes wrong in Saigon and how to avoid it, see [is Ho Chi Minh City safe?](/teach-in-vietnam/is-ho-chi-minh-city-safe).

Your learners' level differs a little too. In the [EF English Proficiency Index 2025](https://news.tuoitre.vn/vietnam-returns-to-global-moderate-english-proficiency-group-ef-103251120163417603.htm), Hanoi scored 532, the highest of the Vietnamese cities listed, against Nha Trang 517, Da Nang 509, Ho Chi Minh City 508 and Hai Phong 506.

Getting around is by motorbike and ride-hailing in every city. Saigon also has [Metro Line 1](https://tuoitre.vn/tp-hcm-chinh-thuc-chot-gia-ve-di-tau-dien-metro-so-1-20241121100826513.htm), open since 22 December 2024 from Ben Thanh to Suoi Tien through 14 stations, with a {{vnd:300000}} monthly pass. In Saigon and Hanoi, Grab has offered an English-speaking GrabBike option since June 2026.

sections.title: Hai Phong, Nha Trang, Can Tho and other cities

blocks.text: Outside the big three, markets are smaller, full-time roles are fewer and the data is thin. On 1 July 2025, [when Vietnam cut its provinces to 34](https://baophapluat.vn/dien-tich-quy-mo-dan-so-23-tinhthanh-pho-moi-sau-sap-xep-post553583.html), Hai Phong and Can Tho absorbed neighbouring provinces and Khanh Hoa, Nha Trang's province, merged with Ninh Thuan, so an ad may name the merged city or province for a campus a long way from the centre.

blocks.text: Some of these jobs come with extras the big cities rarely offer. A [Con Dao island public-school job](https://teast.co/job/full-time-esl-teachers-in-con-dao-island-Al2rPIbW9K4mlgCZNgC5) advertised around September 2026 paid {{vnd:30000000}} a month net for 50–60 teaching hours a month, with school-provided housing, one return flight a school year and a {{vnd:10000000}} completion bonus. In a small city, line up the job before you move, because there may be no second employer if the first one falls through.

items: **Ho Chi Minh City suits a first job.** It has the most employers, the widest choice of job types (centres, kindergartens, public schools, bilingual and international schools) and the easiest switch if a school disappoints. You pay for it in heat and, if you want an expat-style flat, rent.

**Hanoi suits teachers who want seasons and lower central rent.** Hourly rates in 2026 ads match or beat Saigon's, and Numbeo's safety and commute scores are better. Weigh the damp, unheated winter and the winter smog first.

**Da Nang suits experienced teachers who want a smaller, beach city.** Hourly rates are similar, but there are far fewer jobs, some chains ask for 3+ years' experience, and September to December brings storms and floods.
**Hai Phong, Nha Trang and Can Tho suit teachers who want a quieter, more local life** and will secure a job before they move.
**Undecided?** Start in Saigon. It is the easiest place to find work and to move on from later.

blocks.text: Whichever city you choose, the job search works the same way; [finding a teaching job in Vietnam](/teach-in-vietnam/finding-a-teaching-job-in-vietnam) covers where jobs are posted and how to check an employer. Linked teaching jobs on [eno.vn's jobs page](/jobs-vietnam-expats) open the original posting, where you apply.

sections.title: Can you start in one city and move to another?

blocks.text: Yes, but if you change employer, your work permit does not move with you. Under [Decree 219/2025/ND-CP](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/nghi-dinh-219-2025-nd-cp-quy-dinh-ve-nguoi-lao-dong-nuoc-ngoai-tai-viet-nam-407607-d1.html), in force since 7 August 2025, a permit is issued for a specific employer, and working for a different employer needs a new permit, even for the same job. Since [Decision 346/QĐ-BNV](https://www.ey.com/en_vn/technical/tax/tax-and-law-updates/decision-346-qd-bnv-on-the-amendment-and-supplementation-of-administrative-procedures-for-foreign-employees-working-in-vietnam) (24 March 2026) you also re-submit your degree and experience proof, so keep your authenticated documents and certified translations safe. Working for the same employer in another province is different: Decree 219 requires no extra permit, but the employer must notify the authority at least 3 days before you start work there (Art 22(5)); ask the employer to confirm this in writing before a transfer.

The new employer files in the province where its office, branch or business location for the job is. In Ho Chi Minh City that is the Department of Home Affairs for practically every language centre and school ([Decision 6093/QĐ-UBND](https://luatvietnam.vn/lao-dong/quyet-dinh-6093-qd-ubnd-tp-ho-chi-minh-2026-cong-bo-danh-muc-thu-tuc-hanh-chinh-sua-doi-bo-sung-448197-d2.html), 21 September 2026). The employer and the authority have the final word on what your file needs; the [work permit guide](/teach-in-vietnam/vietnam-work-permit-for-english-teachers) covers the process.

Mind your current contract too. On a 12–36-month labour contract you must give at least 30 days' notice to resign, and quitting without proper notice costs half a month's salary plus pay for the missing notice days ([Labour Code Arts. 35 and 40](https://dulieuphapluat.vn/van-ban/lao-dong/bo-luat-lao-dong-2019-45716.html)). Completion bonuses are usually lost if you leave early, so the cheapest time to change city is at the end of a contract.

faqs.q: Does Hanoi pay more than Ho Chi Minh City?
faqs.a: Not by much. In July–October 2026 ads, Hanoi centres offered roughly the same hourly rates as Saigon or slightly more, and guides that claim a fixed Saigon premium are not backed by current ads. Compare written offers, not city averages.

faqs.q: Is Da Nang a good place for a first teaching job?
faqs.a: It is harder than Saigon or Hanoi. There are far fewer jobs, and ILA's 2026 ads ask for at least 3 years' experience for Da Nang, Nha Trang and Vung Tau. Many teachers start in Saigon and move once they have experience.

faqs.q: Which Vietnamese city is cheapest for a teacher?
faqs.a: Among the big three, Hanoi has the cheapest central rent on Numbeo, and Da Nang has slightly lower day-to-day costs. Smaller cities such as Can Tho and Hai Phong look cheaper still, but their data is thin and so are their job markets.

faqs.q: Can I teach in Hoi An?
faqs.a: Hoi An has been part of Da Nang city since the July 2025 merger, so its jobs may be listed under Da Nang. We found no Hoi An pay data and Da Nang's own market is small, so line up a job before you move and check the flood risk of any home you rent.

faqs.q: When is the best time to arrive?
faqs.a: Language centres hire all year, busiest before and during the June–August summer holiday and, by teachers' accounts, slowest from mid-December until Tet, which falls on 6 February 2027. Public-school jobs follow the September to May school year in every city.
